Daily Quiz.question: ১) Who is the Author of " It's a Battlefield"?
Daily Quiz.exp:
It's a Battlefield:
- This is an early novel by Graham Greene, first published in 1934.
- Graham Greene later described it as his "first overtly political novel". Its theme, said Greene, is "the injustice of man's justice.

Graham Greene(2 October 1904 – 3 April 1991):
-In full Henry Graham Greene.
-English novelist, short-story writer, playwright, and journalist whose novels treat life’s moral ambiguities in the context of contemporary political settings.

Notable works:
- Brighton Rock
- The Power and the Glory (1940)
- The End of the Affair
- A Burnt-Out Case
- The Comedians
- Our Man in Havana
-The Quiet American The Human Factor, Stamboul Train.

[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

Daily Quiz.question: ২) 'Aziz and Adela' are the two vital characters from the novel -

Daily Quiz.option2: খ) Where Angels Fear to Tread
Daily Quiz.exp:
A Passage to India:
This is a famous novel which was written by Edward Morgan Forster.

• The important character of this novel:
- Dr. Aziz (Protagonist),
- Mrs. Moore
- Adela Quested,
- Rony Hislop,
- Cyril Fielding,
- Stella Moore.
• Forster's A Passage to India, the main character, Dr. Aziz, is a Moslem doctor living in Chandrapore.

E.M. Forster (1879-1970):
- In full Edward Morgan Forster. British novelist, essayist, and social and literary critic.

Best works:

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) "One Hundred Years of Solitude" is a masterpiece novel written by-

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) Who is one of the Pioneer of Imagism in English Literature?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Ezra Pound:
- He is one of the exponents of Imagism. He wrote a two-line poem as an example of imagist poetry . 
- Here is the poem:
" In a station of the Metro" 
The apparition of these faces in the crowd;
Petals on a wet, black bough.  

Imagist:
- Imagist, any of a group of American and English poets whose poetic program was formulated about 1912 by Ezra Pound—in conjunction with fellow poets Hilda Doolittle (H.D.), Richard Aldington, and F.S. Flint—and was inspired by the critical views of T.E. Hulme, in revolt against the careless thinking and Romantic optimism he saw prevailing.

Source: An ABC of English Literature- Dr M Mofizar Rahman & Britannica.com

The Proposed Roads to Freedom:
- This book contains Bertrand Russell's astute political commentary on anarchism, socialism, and syndicalism.
- Russell begins with a historical overview of socialism and anarchism, the teachings and organizations of Marx and Bakunin, and the syndicalist revolt against socialism.

Bertrand Russell: (1872 – 1970): 
- Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher, logician, mathematician, history writer, social critic, and political activist.
- He was awarded the Nobel prize in literature in 1950.

His notable Works:
- Mysticism and Logic,
- The Analysis of Mind,
- History of Western philosophy,
- Authority and Individual.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman, and Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) "Catherine Barkley" is a character from which novel?
Daily Quiz.exp:
A Farewell to Arms:
- The third novel by Ernest Hemingway, published in 1929.

Plot & main Characters:
- The plot of A Farewell to Arms is fairly straightforward. While working with the Italian ambulance service during World War I (1914–18), the American lieutenant Frederic Henry meets the English nurse Catherine Barkley.
- Although she still mourns the death of her fiancé, who was killed in the war, Catherine encourages Henry’s advances.
After Henry is badly wounded by a trench mortar shell near the Isonzo River in Italy, he is brought to a hospital in Milan, where he is eventually joined by Catherine.
- She tends to him as he recovers. During this time their relationship deepens. Henry admits that he has fallen in love with her.
- Catherine soon becomes pregnant by Henry but refuses to marry him.

Ernest Hemingway (1899 – 1961)
- He is an American Novelist.
- Hew was awarded Nobel Prize in 1954.
Best Works:
- For whom the Bell Tolls,
- The Old Man and the Sea,
- A Farewell to Arms,
- The Sun also Rises,
- Death in the Afternoon
Source: Britannica
